cards.text: Jesus just raised a widow's only son back to life in a town called Nain, and the news spread through Judea and all the surrounding region (Luke 7:11-17). Now it reaches John the Baptist, the prophet who preached a baptism of repentance around the Jordan (Luke 3:3). John's disciples tell him about all these things.

cards.question: John calls two of his disciples and sends them to Jesus with a question. What does John want to know?

answers.text: If Jesus is the One who was to come
If Jesus will come and baptize with him
If Jesus will teach them how to pray

cards.text: The two men find Jesus and repeat John's question word for word: "Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?" Not one word added, not one word dropped, which is more than any group chat has EVER done.

cards.question: True or false: At that very hour, before Jesus answers John's men, He heals many people and gives sight to many who are blind.
Jesus doesn't give John's men a plain yes or no. What does He tell them to report back to John?

answers.text: What they have seen and heard
That John should come and see
That they must wait for a sign

cards.text: Then Jesus spells it out: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear and the dead are raised. John asks a yes or no question, and Jesus sends back a HIGHLIGHT REEL.

cards.question: There's one more thing on Jesus' list. The good news is preached to the ___.
John asked if Jesus is the One who was to come. Jesus ends His reply to John with a blessing. Who does Jesus say is blessed?

answers.text: The one who does not fall away because of Him
The one who has seen His miracles up close
The one who keeps every word of the law

cards.text: After John's messengers leave, Jesus starts talking to the crowds about John and asks, "What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?" Friend, NOBODY hikes out into the wilderness to watch a plant wiggle.

cards.question: Next Jesus asks if the crowds went out to see a man in fine clothes. True or false: Jesus says people who wear elegant clothing and live in luxury are found in the wilderness.

cards.text: Third guess, and Jesus asks it straight: "What then did you go out to see? A prophet?" Then He answers His own question.

cards.question: Jesus asks the crowds if they went out to see a prophet. What is His answer about John?

answers.text: Yes and more than a prophet
No he is only a teacher
Not yet but someday he will be

cards.text: Jesus says John is the one Scripture already wrote about. In that Scripture, God says He will send His messenger ahead.

cards.question: In the Scripture Jesus quotes about John, God's messenger goes ahead to ___ the way.

cards.text: Then Jesus says that among those born of women, there is NO ONE greater than John. That's a greatest of all time title straight from Jesus, but He's not done.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says even the least in the kingdom of God is still not as great as John.

cards.text: All the people who hear this acknowledge God's justice, even the tax collectors. When the TAX COLLECTORS are nodding along, you know something big is going on.

cards.question: The people who hear Jesus, even the tax collectors, acknowledge God's justice. What reason does the passage give?

answers.text: They had paid back what they owed
They had given money to the poor

cards.question: The Pharisees, a strict group of Jewish religious leaders, and the experts in the law reject God's purpose for themselves. Why? They had not been ___ by John.

cards.text: Jesus is still talking to the crowds, and now He asks, "To what, then, can I compare the men of this generation? What are they like?" He's about to answer with a picture.

cards.question: What picture does Jesus use to describe the men of this generation?

cards.text: The children call out to one another about the music they made for the others: they played the flute, and they sang a dirge. Happy song, sad song, these children came with the WHOLE playlist.

cards.question: True or false: In Jesus' picture, the other children dance to the flute but won't weep at the dirge.

cards.text: Then Jesus explains the picture. John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine.

cards.question: John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine. What do people say about him?

cards.text: Then Jesus, the Son of Man, comes eating and drinking, and they call Him a glutton and a drunkard. Friend, that's the coworker who says the office is too cold, so you turn up the heat, and now it's too HOT.

cards.question: Along with glutton and drunkard, people call Jesus a friend of tax collectors and ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus wraps up the whole comparison with one short line about wisdom and her children. Short line, BIG weight.

cards.question: Jesus ends the comparison with this line: But wisdom is ___ by all her children.

findings.problem: Too many choices ask for the next unseen detail rather than an informed inference. The setups do not let the baker reason out the marketplace picture in card 2, the children's exact response in card 4, or the demon accusation in card 6, and card 10 is another unseen-word guess. Most of the stop therefore becomes a guessing game.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Card 9 says only that Jesus' closing line concerns wisdom and her children. It gives no context for what those children do, so the blank asks for the unseen BSB wording 'vindicated' rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
